description: Your coding assistant from Jarvis for Kubuntu: explain, fix, review and document code, write tests, understand compiler errors. Jarvis learns your languages, projects and the solutions that worked.
welcome.history:
Answers you get from Jarvis appear here, so you can open them again.
[Ask Jarvis](command:jarvis.ask)
walk.title: Get started with Jarvis
walk.description: Your local coding assistant: explain, fix, review, test and learn.
walk.connect.title: Connect to Jarvis
walk.connect.text:
The extension talks to the Jarvis app on this computer. When the status bar shows $(hubot) Jarvis, you are connected. Answers need a Claude API key set in Jarvis.
[Open the Jarvis app](command:jarvis.openApp)
walk.ask.title: Ask a question
walk.ask.text:
Press Ctrl+Alt+K, or click Jarvis in the status bar. The open file goes along as context.
[Ask about the code](command:jarvis.ask)
walk.selection.title: Work with a selection
walk.selection.text:
Select code and right-click → Jarvis: explain it, fix it, write tests or add comments. A fix can be compared with your code before it replaces the selection.
[All Jarvis actions](command:jarvis.menu)
walk.errors.title: Understand errors
walk.errors.text:
On a red squiggle, open the light bulb (Ctrl+.) and pick "Jarvis: explain and fix this error". Or review the whole file.
[Review this file](command:jarvis.review)
walk.learn.title: Teach Jarvis
walk.learn.text:
Rate answers with 👍 / 👎. Good solutions become lessons Jarvis reuses — even offline. Select your own working code and teach it to Jarvis.
[Teach a solution](command:jarvis.teach)
cfg.learn: Tell Jarvis which languages and projects you work on and which errors you hit, so it learns your programming (stays on this computer; code is sent only by your commands).
cfg.lightbulb: Offer "Jarvis: explain and fix this error" in the light bulb on errors.
cfg.socket: Path to the Jarvis daemon socket. Empty: $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/jarvis-ide.sock.
